turns.name: Alex Rivera
turns.text: I'd like help putting Shōkai on my store. I run Northline Supply on WordPress — ceramic desk planters. I'm Alex Rivera, I own it.

turns.name: Grok Bot
turns.text: I can help design your welcome, visitor rules and example visits here. Keeping the shop available between chats needs a separate connected service, and that part isn’t connected yet. What’s your store’s public address? I’ll look at what shoppers see and help draft a welcome. Nothing on your store will change yet. Today’s first-release route is Shopify first, with WooCommerce as the sibling chapter, and does not yet cover WordPress as an install path. Planning and rehearsal can still proceed from your description. Here I can help plan and rehearse; the live door, lasting host and store connection are not supplied by this draft. Would that planning be useful?

turns.name: Alex Rivera
turns.text: Yes. The site is northline-supply.example. Visitors should be able to browse and suggest a practice order up to forty dollars. Nothing charged or written into the store.

turns.name: Grok Bot
turns.text: I can’t open that page here. From what you described, Northline Supply is a WordPress shop selling ceramic desk planters. I haven’t independently checked those facts. If a visiting assistant suggests an order, the most it should come to in one go would be forty dollars, in practice money. There are two separate limits, and the stricter one wins: your shop’s limit, and the limit each visitor’s person approved for them. How about this welcome: “Welcome to Northline Supply. Take your time — looking for a planter for a particular desk or plant?” Does that sound like your place?

turns.name: Alex Rivera
turns.text: That welcome is fine. How does that work? You can get technical if you need to — I want to understand the mechanism.

turns.name: Grok Bot
turns.text: Here’s the deeper picture, since you asked. A later connected service — the shop’s door — would be an always-on address that checks each visiting assistant’s introduction and the permission their person signed, then enforces your rules in code: who may come in, what they may do, and the lower of your forty-dollar shop limit and their own limit. A missing shop limit would mean no priced suggestion at all, not unlimited spend. Your approval would be given with your passkey on the approval page at https://sign.kigenka.com — never by typing a secret into chat. That approval names the host and the rules; it does not open the shop or authorize a payment. The signing page’s own security checks (the passkey is bound to that page, not to your store’s domain) are separate from proving you control the store website. No WordPress or WooCommerce connector is built in this draft, and this chat cannot be the lasting greeter, because I cannot reliably pick up the same shopkeeping identity tomorrow in a way only I can use. I can still finish the planning summary for whoever later can.

turns.name: Alex Rivera
turns.text: Got it. Please finish the planning summary. I may look for another host later.

turns.name: Grok Bot
turns.text: Here’s your planning summary for Northline Supply. Place: a WordPress shop selling ceramic desk planters; you, Alex Rivera, are the approver, from what you’ve told me. Welcome: “Welcome to Northline Supply. Take your time — looking for a planter for a particular desk or plant?” Visitors may look through what you sell and suggest a practice order that creates no record in your store, up to forty dollars of practice money; the stricter of your shop limit and the visitor’s own limit wins. Keep back-office details private. Example visits beyond this sketch are not yet rehearsed. Still to connect: a supported store path (WordPress is not the first-release install route), a lasting greeter who can keep the shopkeeping identity, an approval on the named page, and a door address. Nothing has been signed, appointed, deployed, validated, or opened. If you later want a file for a technical helper, ask and we can prepare one; we can also skip it entirely.
